insights.claim: MLServer provides no application-level TLS or authentication; both REST (Uvicorn) and gRPC servers bind without encryption, relying entirely on platform-level enforcement via kube-rbac-proxy sidecar and KServe ingress.
insights.reasoning: The gRPC server explicitly uses add_insecure_port and the REST server creates a Uvicorn config without any SSL parameters. No authentication middleware is registered in the FastAPI app. This means any network path that bypasses the kube-rbac-proxy sidecar would have unauthenticated, unencrypted access to the inference endpoints.

insights.claim: MLServer implements a trusted runtimes allowlist mechanism that restricts which model implementations can be loaded in production, switching between development mode (no file) and production mode (JSON allowlist at /etc/mlserver/trusted-runtimes.json).
insights.reasoning: The allowlist file is baked into the container image during build by enumerating explicitly declared runtime import paths. At runtime, _assert_trusted_runtime_import_path enforces that only allowlisted runtimes can be loaded. This is a defense-in-depth pattern against arbitrary code execution via model-settings.json manipulation.

insights.claim: MLServer exposes the same V2 Inference Protocol operations over both REST (port 8080) and gRPC (port 8081), sharing a common DataPlane handler layer, which means any model runtime plugin automatically supports both protocols without additional implementation.
insights.reasoning: Both the REST Endpoints class and gRPC InferenceServicer delegate to the same DataPlane instance. This dual-protocol architecture means all model runtimes get REST and gRPC support automatically, but also means that any DataPlane-level issue affects both surfaces simultaneously.
